Q: Inner join vs Where A:

There is no difference between the two. Look at these two tables:

CREATE TABLE table1 (
  id INT,
  name VARCHAR(20)
);

CREATE TABLE table2 (
  id INT,
  name VARCHAR(20)
);

The execution plan for the query using the inner join:

-- with inner join

EXPLAIN PLAN FOR
SELECT * FROM table1 t1
INNER JOIN table2 t2 ON t1.id = t2.id;

SELECT *
FROM TABLE (DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY);

-- 0 select statement
-- 1 hash join (access("T1"."ID"="T2"."ID"))
-- 2 table access full table1
-- 3 table access full table2

And the execution plan for the query using a WHERE clause.

-- with where clause

EXPLAIN PLAN FOR
SELECT * FROM table1 t1, table2 t2
WHERE t1.id = t2.id;

SELECT *
FROM TABLE (DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY);

-- 0 select statement
-- 1 hash join (access("T1"."ID"="T2"."ID"))
-- 2 table access full table1
-- 3 table access full table2

Q: Reloading a local Julia package (without Revise) A:

That "reload" in "Creating Packages" seems to mean "restart the julia session and import again", after reading this "Developing Packages" warning:

https://pkgdocs.julialang.org/v1/managing-packages/#Warning-70c005ff86fb3355

Warning

A package can only be loaded once per Julia session. If you have run import Example in the current Julia session, you will have to restart Julia to see the changes to Example. Revise.jl can make this process significantly more pleasant, but setting it up is beyond the scope of this guide.

Q: edit meta comment tag of an mkv file A:

You can use ffmpeg to add a comment or other metadata to an .mkv file, so you don't need to first create an XML file.

The disadvantage is that it doesn't add the comment to an existing file, but creates a copy of the file with the added comment and/or other metadata. But video, audio, subtitles etc are copied without re-encoding.

Example (using variables):

ffmpeg -i "$my_mkv_in" -c copy -map 0 -metadata title="$My_Title" -metadata artist="$Artist" -metadata comment="$Comment" "$mkv_new"

Q: How to use Postgres timestamp ranges in Rust with time-rs, especially NULL and (-)infinity? A:

It is not possible with time.rs, there are no trait implementations to convert tstzrange to Option<Range<time::OffsetDateTime>> and back.

Options:

  1. Do not use tstzrange, use two timestamptz columns instead with appropriate constraints
  2. Refactor your code to use chrono-rs instead of time-rs, and enable with-chrono-0_4 on postgres_range-rs
  3. Use a third party library that does implement ranges on top of postgres-rs, like sqlx-rs which has PgRange.
